title: Wolf and Thorn Revisited
premise: Bram Okafor, youngest ledger-keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things, inherits a dying stranger's map to the Court Beneath the Mountain, where the guild's founder sold her own soul generations ago to buy the guild its power. Hunted by the usurper Veyran's inquisitors and shadowed by Sera, a thorn-sworn knight ordered to retrieve the map at any cost, Bram discovers the 'impossible things' the guild trades are fragments of stolen souls — including his own mother's. As Veyran's armies march on the free cities, Bram and Sera must choose between duty and each other, descending beneath the mountain to bargain with the court itself. In the end Bram returns the founder's soul to free the guild from its corrupted bargain, Sera breaks her thorn-oath to stand with him, and together they unmake the court's claim — though Bram pays with his memories of her, a loss love must slowly reclaim.
about_author: Felix Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing merchant ledgers in port cities before turning to fiction, a past that haunts his obsession with records, debts, and what paper can hold. He writes fantasy about ordinary people trapped inside other people's bargains.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the guildhall of Ashfall, Bram balances accounts of impossible trades while the guild's elders wither and die one by one. A stranger collapses at the counting desk and presses a bloodstained map into Bram's hands, whispering that the debt is due. Emotional beat: quiet dread as routine curdles into inheritance he never wanted.

chapters.title: Thorn-Sworn
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Knight-commander Sera receives her order: recover the map, kill the courier if needed. She tracks Bram through Ashfall's rain-slick markets but hesitates when she sees him weep over the stranger's body. Emotional beat: duty grinding against a conscience she has buried for years.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Deciphering the map, Bram finds the guild's oldest ledger sealed behind the vault wall: entries recording souls sold to the Court Beneath the Mountain, the last entry his mother's name. The guildhall burns that night — inquisitors' work. Emotional beat: betrayal and grief fusing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath the Cities
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing the fire, Bram is cornered by Sera — who instead of killing him proposes an uneasy alliance, lying to her superiors about his death. They descend into the underways toward the mountain. Emotional beat: wary trust kindling between enemies bound by mutual lies.

chapters.title: Veyran's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the free city of Callowmere they learn the usurper Veyran has been buying soul-fragments through guild intermediaries for years, building an army that cannot feel fear or mercy. Bram realizes the map leads to the source of Veyran's power. Emotional beat: horror at seeing his own trade's logic scaled into tyranny.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Thorn-captains catch up to them; Sera duels her former mentor to buy Bram time and is branded oathbreaker, her thorn-brand now burning her alive by degrees. She confesses she was ordered to kill him from the start. Emotional beat: love admitted too late, paid for in flesh.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. They reach the court, a cathedral of contracts where the founder's soul hangs caged in glass. The court's steward offers Bram a trade: the souls he wants for the map and his own name — his identity, written out of existence. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by everything he has already lost.

chapters.title: Armies of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Above ground, Veyran's hollow soldiers breach Callowmere's walls; refugees flood the passes as the free cities' last alliance crumbles. Sera, dying of the brand, begs Bram to take the steward's deal and save himself. Emotional beat: despair at its lowest ebb, the cost of every choice made visible.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Bargain
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Climax. Instead of trading, Bram exploits the one law the court cannot break: a debt honestly audited must be voided. He presents the founder's original contract, proves the guild overpaid, and demands restitution — every stolen soul returned. The court shatters; Veyran's army collapses mid-march as their purchased souls tear free. Emotional beat: triumph through bookkeeping turned weapon, courage disguised as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Wolf and Thorn
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Resolution. The guild rewrites itself around freely given gifts rather than taken souls; Sera survives, her brand cooled to a scar. Bram, having paid part of the price, remembers nothing of their journey — but keeps a ledger entry in his own hand reading 'worth it.' Sera begins teaching him who she is. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope, love choosing to begin again.
